paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering a new era of G protein-coupled receptor ("GPCR") oral small molecule drug discovery powered by our proprietary Native Complex Platform®. Our industrial-scale platform aims to unlock the full potential of GPCR therapies and has led to the discovery and development of our deep pipeline of product candidates focused initially on treating patients in three therapeutic areas: endocrinology, immunology and inflammation, and metabolic diseases.

GPCRs are the largest and most diverse family of cell membrane receptors and regulate physiological processes in nearly every organ system of the human body. Due to their significant role in human diseases, GPCRs have been the most productive target class in drug discovery history, accounting for approximately one-third of all FDA-approved drugs, representing approximately 500 products with combined global revenue of approximately $125 billion in 2023. Despite the pharmacological and commercial success of GPCR-targeted agents, about 75% of potential GPCR therapeutic targets remain undrugged. For certain validated GPCRs, novel binding pockets may exist that could offer enhanced therapeutic benefits. Each step in GPCR activation involves subtle conformational changes that have been historically challenging to reproduce outside of a cell. The inability to isolate GPCR proteins in their native functional form outside of a cellular context has prevented scientists from leveraging some of the state-of-the-art technologies that have revolutionized drug discovery in other major target classes over the past decade. This complex challenge has limited GPCR drug discovery, particularly the development of novel oral small molecules, such as agonists for peptide GPCRs and allosteric modulators.

Our proprietary Native Complex Platform® replicates the natural structure, function, and dynamics of GPCRs outside of cells at an industrial scale for, as we believe it, the first time. Our foundational technologies enable us to isolate, purify, and reconstitute full-length, properly folded GPCR proteins within ternary complexes with ligands and transducer proteins in a lipid bilayer that mimics the cell membrane. We then apply state-of-the-art discovery tools and technologies to these defined and tunable protein complexes to structurally design, screen for, and optimize potential product candidates. Leveraging our platform, we conduct GPCR oral small molecule drug discovery using an industrialized and iterative structure-based drug design approach for a diverse collection of GPCR targets. Our Native Complex Platform® is designed to enable us to target specific GPCRs, uncover novel binding pockets for validated receptors, and pursue a wide spectrum of pharmacologies, including agonists (which activate GPCR signaling), antagonists (which inhibit GPCR signaling), and allosteric modulators (which either increase or decrease the degree of GPCR activation by endogenous ligands) to affect GPCR signaling in different ways to achieve desired therapeutic effects.

We are advancing a deep portfolio of oral small molecule GPCR-targeted programs with novel mechanistic approaches to treat diseases across multiple therapeutic areas for patients with significant unmet needs. Our wholly-owned pipeline is focused initially on three therapeutic areas: endocrinology, immunology and inflammation, and metabolic diseases. We intend to evaluate opportunities in other major therapeutic areas, such as neurology, women's health, cardiovascular, and respiratory disease.

GPCRs regulate physiological processes in nearly every organ system of the human body and are the most targeted drug class due to their significant role in human diseases and their pharmacological tractability. Nearly one-third of all FDA-approved drugs in the United States, representing approximately 500 products, target GPCR-associated pathways. In fact, GPCR-related drugs comprise approximately 27% of global pharmaceutical sales.

GPCRs are proteins that span the cell membrane seven times, and their primary function is to recognize extracellular substances, or ligands, and transmit signals across the cell membrane to the inside of the cell. Ligand binding induces conformational changes in GPCRs, forming complexes with signal transducers, including G proteins. These transducers interact with second messengers, modulating various cellular processes. Certain GPCR ligands are capable of activating multiple pathways through different transducers, leading to diverse physiological and pathological effects.

GPCRs constitute the largest and most diverse family of cell membrane receptors, with around 800 identified members. GPCRs are key therapeutic targets due to their vital roles in a variety of physiologic processes including immune regulation, nervous system transmission, mood and behavior regulation, sensory transmission, and maintaining cardiovascular and gastrointestinal homeostasis. Despite the pharmacological and commercial success of GPCR-targeted agents, a majority of GPCR therapeutic targets remain undrugged. Each step in GPCR activation involves subtle conformational changes that have been historically challenging to reproduce outside of a cell. The inability to isolate GPCR proteins in their native functional form outside of a cellular context has prevented scientists from leveraging some of the state-of-the-art technologies that have revolutionized drug discovery in other major target classes over the past decade. This complex challenge has limited GPCR drug discovery, particularly the development of novel oral small molecules, such as agonists for peptide GPCRs and allosteric modulators.

To date, drug discovery has been highly concentrated on a small number of GPCRs. More than 70% of current GPCR-related drugs target only six subfamilies of GPCRs. There are about 400 known non-olfactory GPCRs, each represented as a branch on the phylogenetic tree in Figure 1 below.

Today, approximately 75% of potential GPCR therapeutic targets remain undrugged, representing significant opportunity to address a vast range of therapeutic areas and diseases. And, even for certain validated GPCRs, novel binding pockets may exist that could offer enhanced therapeutic benefits.

In the past decade, drug discovery across various target classes has been revolutionized by state-of-the-art tools and technologies, including structure-based drug design, computational docking, and DNA-encoded libraries ("DELs"). However, the utilization of these technologies has been limited for discovering oral small molecules targeting GPCRs due to the inability to isolate functional native GPCR proteins outside of a cellular context.

With our proprietary Native Complex Platform®, we can purify GPCRs outside of cells and reconstitute them into fully functional ternary complexes with transducer proteins (e.g., G proteins, beta-arrestins) and ligands (endogenous or synthetic), all housed within a well-defined lipid bilayer environment. These Native Complexes are full-length, properly folded GPCRs that retain their natural structure, function, and dynamics. We then apply state-of-the-art discovery tools and technologies to these defined and tunable protein complexes to structurally design, screen for, and optimize potential product candidates. Leveraging our platform, we are advancing a new approach to GPCR drug discovery, designed to expand the landscape of druggable GPCR targets with novel oral small molecule medicines for patients.

Our Native Complex Platform® is powered by a suite of tools and technologies that we have optimized and integrated into a proprietary and industrialized workflow, forming an efficient and iterative discovery process for identification and optimization of novel small molecule product candidates targeting high-value GPCRs, including:

• Native Complex biochemistry and structural biology: Our Native Complexes reconstitute native GPCR function in a purified biochemical format, enabling efficient high-resolution, three-dimensional structure determination using cryogenic electron microscopy ("cryo-EM"). This reveals receptor binding pockets that we can target with a range of pharmacologies (e.g., agonists, antagonists, and allosteric modulators) as well as novel insights into mechanisms for GPCR modulation.

• Native Complex-driven hit identification and optimization: We virtually screen our GPCR structures against ultra-large-scale computational databases containing billions of candidate molecules to identify the most promising small molecule compounds that bind in pockets on the GPCR structure. We use technologies, including DELs, to screen billions of candidate molecules simultaneously and have developed proprietary technologies to discover and optimize compounds with a variety of modes of action. Additionally, we use our proprietary Native Complex biochemical screens in our hit identification and optimization processes.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our financial statements and the related notes appearing at the end of this Annual Report and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," before deciding to invest in our common stock. If any of the events or developments described below were to occur, our business, prospects, operating results and financial condition could suffer materially, the trading price of our common stock could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also adversely affect our business. This Annual Report also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors, including the risks described below. See the section titled "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

Pharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company with a limited operating history, which may make it difficult to evaluate the success of our business to date and assess our future viability. Since our inception in December 2019, we have focused primarily on organizing and staffing our company, business planning, establishing our intellectual property portfolio, raising capital, developing our proprietary and structure-based drug discovery platform, identifying and developing our product candidates, conducting research and preclinical studies, including IND-enabling studies, initiating and conducting clinical trials, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. Our approach to the discovery and development of product candidates based on our Native Complex Platform® is unproven, and we do not know whether we will be able to develop any product candidates that succeed in clinical development or commercially. Other than SEP-631, all of our current product candidates and development programs are in preclinical development or in the drug discovery stages. Accordingly, we have not yet successfully completed any advanced clinical trials, demonstrated an ability to successfully obtain regulatory approvals, manufactured commercial-scale product, or arranged for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conducted sales and marketing activities necessary for successful product commercialization. Consequently, any predictions made about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a history of successfully developing and commercializing pharmaceutical products.

We have no products approved for commercial sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales to date, and we continue to incur significant research and development and other expenses related to our preclinical and clinical development and ongoing operations. As a result, we are not profitable and have incurred significant losses since our inception, with the exception of the year ended December 31, 2023, and negative cash flows from operating activities and capital expenditures and expect to continue to incur significant and increasing operating losses for at least the next several years. If our product candidates are not successfully developed and approved, we may never generate any significant revenue. For the year ended December 31, 2025, our net loss was $48.9 million. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $167.3 million. Substantially all of our losses have resulted from expenses incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. All of our product candidates will require substantial additional development time and resources before we would be able to apply for or receive marketing approvals and begin generating revenue from product sales. We expect to continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future, and we expect that our expenses will increase substantially as we continue our development of, seek marketing approval for and potentially commercialize any of our product candidates, recruit and maintain key personnel and seek to identify, assess, acquire, in-license or develop additional product candidates.

Even if we succeed in developing and obtaining marketing approval for one or more of our product candidates, we may never generate revenue that is significant enough to achieve profitability. If we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis and we will continue to incur substantial research and development and other expenditures to develop and market additional product candidates. Our failure to become and remain profitable could decrease the value of our common stock and impair our ability to raise capital, maintain our research and development efforts, expand our business or continue our operations.

We will require substantial additional funding in order to finance our operations. If we are unable to raise additional capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, we may be forced to delay, reduce, or terminate certain of our research and product development programs, future commercialization efforts or other operations.

The development of pharmaceutical product candidates, including conducting preclinical studies and clinical trials, is a very time-consuming, capital-intensive and uncertain process that takes years to complete. Our operations have consumed substantial amounts of cash since inception, and we expect our expenses to increase in connection with our ongoing activities, particularly as we identify, continue the research and development of, initiate and conduct clinical trials of, and seek regulatory approval for any product candidates we may identify. In addition, if we obtain regulatory approval for any product candidates we may identify, we expect to incur significant commercialization expenses related to product sales, marketing, manufacturing, and distribution to the extent that such sales, marketing, manufacturing, and distribution are not the responsibility of a collaborator. Because the outcome of any clinical trial or preclinical study is highly uncertain, we cannot reasonably estimate the actual amount of capital necessary to successfully complete the development and commercialization of our product candidates. Other unanticipated costs may also arise. Furthermore, we expect to incur additional costs associated with operating as a public company. Accordingly, we will need to obtain substantial additional funding in connection with our continuing operations. If we are unable to raise capital when needed or on acceptable terms, we would be forced to delay, reduce, or eliminate our research and product development programs, future commercialization efforts or other operations.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於透過我們專有的Native Complex Platform®技術，開創G蛋白偶聯受體（"GPCR"）口服小分子藥物發現的新時代。我們的工業規模平台旨在發揮GPCR治療的全部潛力，並已促成我們深具潛力的產品候選藥物開發管道，初期專注於治療三個治療領域的患者：內分泌學、免疫學與發炎，以及代謝疾病。

GPCRs為細胞膜受體中最大且最為多樣的家族，並調節人體幾乎每個器官系統的生理過程。由於其在人類疾病中的重要角色，GPCRs為藥物發現歷史上最具生產力的目標類別，約佔美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准藥物的三分之一，約500種產品，2023年全球總營收約為125十億美元。儘管GPCR目標藥物在藥理學與商業上取得成功，約有75%的潛在GPCR治療目標尚未有藥物。對於某些已驗證的GPCRs，可能存在新的結合位點，可提供增強的治療效益。GPCR活化過程中的每一步都涉及微小的構象變化，這在過去很難在細胞外重現。無法在細胞外環境中分離出具有原生功能的GPCR蛋白質，已阻礙科學家利用過去十年在其他主要目標類別中革新藥物發現的先進技術。這個複雜的挑戰已限制GPCR藥物發現，特別是新型口服小分子藥物的開發，例如肽GPCR的激動劑與別構調節劑。

我們專有的Native Complex Platform®技術可在工業規模下，重現GPCRs在細胞外的自然結構、功能與動態，據我們的信念，這是首次實現。我們的基礎技術使我們能夠在三元複合體中分離、純化並重新組裝完整的、正確摺疊的GPCR蛋白質，與配體及轉導蛋白結合，並在模擬細胞膜的脂質雙層中進行。我們隨後應用最先進的發現工具與技術，對這些明確且可調節的蛋白質複合體進行結構設計、篩選並優化潛在產品候選藥物。透過我們的平台，我們使用工業化且迭代的結構基藥物設計方法，針對多種GPCR目標進行GPCR口服小分子藥物發現。我們的Native Complex Platform®設計用以使我們能針對特定GPCRs，揭露已驗證受體的新結合位點，並追求廣泛的藥理學範疇，包括激動劑（活化GPCR信號）、拮抗劑（抑制GPCR信號）以及別構調節劑（增強或降低內源性配體的GPCR活化程度），以不同方式影響GPCR信號，達到所需的治療效果。
我們正在推進一項深具潛力的口服小分子GPCR目標藥物開發管道，透過創新機制方法，用以治療多個治療領域中具有重大未滿足醫療需求的患者。我們的自有藥物開發管道初期專注於三個治療領域：內分泌學、免疫學與發炎，以及代謝疾病。我們有意評估其他主要治療領域的機會，例如神經學、婦女健康、心血管疾病及呼吸系統疾病。
GPCRs調節人體幾乎每個器官系統的生理過程，並因在人類疾病中的重要角色及藥理學可行性，成為最受關注的藥物目標類別。美國約有三分之一的FDA批准藥物，約500種產品，針對GPCR相關路徑。事實上，GPCR相關藥物約佔全球製藥銷售的27%。
GPCRs為跨細胞膜七次的蛋白質，其主要功能為識別細胞外物質，或配體，並將訊號傳遞至細胞內。配體結合會引發GPCRs的構象變化，形成與訊號轉導蛋白（包括G蛋白）的複合體。這些轉導蛋白會與第二信使互動，調節各種細胞過程。某些GPCR配體有能力透過不同的轉導蛋白激活多條路徑，導致多樣的生理與病理效果。

GPCRs為細胞膜受體中最大且最為多樣的家族，約有800種已識別的成員。GPCRs因在多種生理過程中的關鍵角色，包括免疫調節、神經系統傳導、情緒與行為調節、感測傳導，以及維持心血管與消化系統的內在平衡，而成為重要的治療目標。儘管GPCR目標藥物在藥理學與商業上取得成功，大多數GPCR治療目標仍尚未有藥物。GPCR活化過程中的每一步都涉及微小的構象變化，這在過去很難在細胞外重現。無法在細胞外環境中分離出具有原生功能的GPCR蛋白質，已阻礙科學家利用過去十年在其他主要目標類別中革新藥物發現的先進技術。這個複雜的挑戰已限制GPCR藥物發現，特別是新型口服小分子藥物的開發，例如肽GPCR的激動劑與別構調節劑。
截至目前為止，藥物發現高度集中於少數GPCRs。目前超過70%的GPCR相關藥物僅針對六個GPCR亞家族。約有400種已知的非嗅覺GPCRs，每種都以圖1下方的演化樹中的一個分支來代表。
今日，約 75% 的 GPCR 潤滑劑治療目標尚未被開發，代表著針對廣泛治療領域與疾病的顯著機會。此外，即使對於某些已驗證的 GPCRs，仍可能存在新的結合口袋，這些口袋可能提供增強的治療效益。
過去十年，各類目標類別的藥物發現已因最先進的工具與技術而產生革命性變革，包括結構基準藥物設計、計算機 docking 以及 DNA 編碼庫（"DELs"）。然而，這些技術的應用在發現針對 GPCRs 的口服小分子藥物時受到限制，原因是無法在細胞環境之外隔離功能性 GPCR 蛋白質。

透過我們專利的 Native Complex 平台®，我們可以將 GPCRs 從細胞中純化，並重新組裝為具有轉導蛋白（例如 G 蛋白、beta-arrestins）與配體（內源性或合成性）的完整功能三元複合體，所有這些皆位於明確界定的脂質雙層環境中。這些 Native Complexes 是完整長度、正確摺疊的 GPCRs，保留其自然結構、功能與動態。我們隨後應用最先進的發現工具與技術，針對這些明確且可調控的蛋白質複合體進行結構設計、篩選與優化潛在產品候選物。透過我們的平台，我們正在推動 GPCR 藥物發現的新方法，旨在擴展可開發 GPCR 目標的範圍，為患者提供新的口服小分子藥物。
我們的 Native Complex 平台® 由一組我們已優化並整合至專利且工業化的流程中的工具與技術所驅動，形成一種高效且可迭代的發現流程，用以識別與優化針對高價值 GPCRs 的新小分子產品候選物，包括：
• Native Complex 生化與結構生物學：我們的 Native Complexes 在純化生化格式中重組 GPCR 的天然功能，使我們能透過冷凍電子顯微鏡（"cryo-EM"）進行高效高解析度、三維結構確定。這揭示了我們可針對的受體結合口袋，以及各種藥理學（例如：激動劑、拮抗劑與別構調節劑）以及 GPCR 調節機制的新見解。

• Native Complex 驅動的命中識別與優化：我們將 GPCR 結構虛擬篩選至包含十億個候選分子的超大規模計算資料庫，以識別最具有潛力的小分子化合物，這些化合物會結合在 GPCR 結構的口袋中。我們使用技術，包括 DELs，同時篩選十億個候選分子，並已發展出專利技術以發現並優化具有多種作用機制的化合物。此外，我們在命中識別與優化流程中使用我們專利的 Native Complex 生化篩選。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們經審計之財務報表及相關附註資料一併參考。本討論及其他部分之內容包含基於目前信念、計畫與預期之展望性陳述，涉及未來事件及我們未來財務表現之風險、不確定性與假設，例如我們計畫、目標、預期、意圖、預測與預測之陳述。我們實際結果與特定事件之時程可能與這些展望性陳述所討論者有重大差異，原因包括，但不僅限於，於本年度報告「風險因素」節中所列述之因素及其他因素。我們歷史結果未必能代表未來任何期間之結果，您應謹慎閱讀「風險因素」節，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與我們展望性陳述有重大差異之重要因素。請同時參閱「關於展望性陳述之特別說明」節。
我們是一家臨牀階段生物技術公司，正開創GPCR口服小分子藥物之新時代，此藥物係由我們專屬之Native Complex Platform®所發現。我們的工業規模平台旨在釋放GPCR治療之全部潛力，並已導致我們發現並開發出深具規模之藥物候選品，最初專注於治療三個治療領域之病患：內分泌學、免疫學與發炎，以及代謝疾病。

我們專屬之Native Complex Platform®能在工業規模下，複製GPCR在細胞外之自然結構、功能與動態，據我們相信，這是首次實現。我們的基礎技術使我們能從GPCR中分離、純化並重新組裝完整的、正確摺疊之GPCR蛋白質，於包含配體與傳導蛋白之三元複合體中，於模擬細胞膜之脂質雙層中。我們隨後應用最先進之發現工具與技術，針對這些定義明確且可調節之蛋白質複合體，進行結構設計、篩選及優化潛在產品候選品。透過我們的平台，我們使用工業化與迭代式結構基藥物設計方法，針對多種GPCR目標進行GPCR口服小分子藥物之發現。我們的Native Complex Platform®設計用以使我們能針對特定GPCR，揭露已驗證受體之新結合口袋，並追求廣泛之藥理學範疇，包括活化GPCR信號之激動劑（agonists）、抑制GPCR信號之拮抗劑（antagonists），以及增強或降低內源性配體之GPCR活化程度之別構調節劑（allosteric modulators），以不同方式影響GPCR信號，以達成所需之治療效果。
我們正在推進一項深具規模之口服小分子GPCR目標計畫組合，以創新機制方式治療多個治療領域之病患，這些病患具有重大未滿足之醫療需求。我們自有之產品線如下圖所示。
我們於2019年12月在特拉華州成立，公司名稱為GPCR NewCo, Inc。2021年6月，我們將公司名稱更為Septerna, Inc。我們總部設於美國加州南舊金山。

自我們成立以來，我們已產生顯著之營運虧損，除了2023年12月31日結算年度外。我們至今之收入完全來自研究服務。自成立以來，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入於公司組織與人力配置、業務規劃、籌資、開發我們專屬之結構基藥物發現平台、識別與發現產品候選品、建立我們之智慧財產權組合、進行研究與臨牀前研究，包括新藥申請（IND）啟動研究、啟動與進行臨牀試驗、建立與第三方之製造安排以製造產品候選品及相關原料、以及為這些運作提供一般及行政支援。我們尚未有任何產品獲准上市銷售，也尚未產生任何產品銷售收入。此外，我們預期在成功完成開發並取得行銷核准之前，不會產生來自商業產品銷售之收入。我們產生產品收入之能力，將取決於我們成功開發並最終商業化一個或多個產品候選品之能力。

本公司淨損失為 48.9 百萬美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年淨損失 71.8 百萬美元相比。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 167.3 百萬美元。自成立以來，本公司每年均發生淨損失，除了 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年。本公司預期將持續在可預見的未來發生淨損失。本公司淨損失可能因運營活動的時間安排及支出而顯著波動。
我們預期在接下來數年持續產生顯著且增加之淨營運虧損，因為我們：
• 繼續推動我們的產品候選藥物通過臨牀前研究並進入臨牀試驗；
• 吸引、僱用並留住更多人力資源；
• 繼續作為上市公司運作，包括符合美國證券交易委員會（SEC）及任何上市交易之國家證券交易所規則與規範的費用、法律、會計、保險費用、投資者關係活動及其他行政與專業服務費用；
• 繼續我們的研究與開發努力，並擴充產品候選藥物的管線；
• 收購、發現、驗證並開發更多產品候選藥物；• 為我們的臨牀前研究與臨牀試驗製造所需物料；
• 取得、維持、擴展並保護我們的智慧財產權組合；• 實施作業、財務與資訊管理系統；

paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括財務報表及附於本年度報告末尾的相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」的章節，再決定是否投資本公司普通股。若下列所描述的任何事件或發展發生，將可能使本公司的業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況受到重大影響，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司目前認為不重要，也可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。本年度報告中亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。本公司實際結果可能與展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因在於多種因素，包括下列所描述的風險。請參閱標題為「特別注意展望性陳述」的章節。

藥物產品開發是一項高度投機性的業務，並涉及相當程度的風險。本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，營運歷史有限，這可能使評估本公司業務至今的成功程度與評估本公司未來的生存能力變得困難。自本公司於2019年12月成立以來，我們主要致力於組織與僱用員工、業務規劃、建立智慧財產權組合、籌集資金、發展專屬且基於結構的藥物發現平台、識別與開發產品候選物、進行研究與臨牀前研究，包括IND啟動研究、啟動與進行臨牀試驗，以及為這些業務提供一般及行政支援。本公司針對基於Native Complex Platform®的產品候選物進行發現與開發的策略尚未經過驗證，我們不知道是否能成功開發任何在臨牀開發中成功的產品候選物。除了SEP-631之外，我們目前所有產品候選物與開發計畫皆處於臨牀前開發階段或藥物發現階段。因此，我們尚未成功完成任何進階臨牀試驗，也未證明能成功取得監管核准、製造商業規模產品、或安排第三方代為製造，或進行成功產品商業化所需的銷售與行銷活動。因此，任何關於本公司未來成功或生存能力的預測可能不如我們有成功開發與商業化藥物產品的歷史時那麼準確。

本公司目前尚無產品獲得商業銷售許可，且截至目前為止尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，且本公司持續產生與預臨牀及臨牀開發及持續營運相關的重大研究與開發及其他費用。因此，本公司尚未獲利，且自成立以來持續產生重大虧損，除2023年12月31日財務年度外，並產生負的營運活動現金流及資本支出，且預期將持續產生重大且日益增加的營運虧損，至少持續數年。若本公司產品候選藥物未能成功開發並獲得批准，本公司可能永遠無法產生任何重大收入。2025年12月31日財務年度，本公司淨虧損為48.9 百萬美元。2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為167.3 百萬美元。本公司幾乎所有虧損均來自與研究與開發計畫相關的費用，以及與營運相關的一般及行政費用。本公司所有產品候選藥物在能夠申請或獲得市場批准並開始從產品銷售中產生收入之前，均需進行大量額外的開發時間與資源。本公司預期將持續產生重大虧損，且預期本公司費用將大幅增加，因本公司持續進行產品候選藥物的開發，尋求市場批准並可能商業化任何產品候選藥物，招募及留住關鍵人員，並尋求識別、評估、取得、授權進口或開發其他產品候選藥物。
即使我們成功開發並取得一個或多個產品候選物的市場核准，我們可能永遠無法產生足夠的收入以達到獲利。若我們確實達到獲利，我們可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的獲利能力，且我們將持續產生重大研究與開發及其他費用，以開發與行銷更多產品候選物。我們未能成為並持續保持獲利，將降低本公司普通股的價值，並影響我們籌資能力、維持研究與開發努力、擴大業務或繼續運作的能力。
我們將需要大量額外資金以支應運作。若我們無法在需要時以可接受的條件或完全無法籌集額外資金，我們可能被迫延遲、減少或終止某些研究與產品開發計畫、未來商業化努力或其他運作。

藥物產品候選物的開發，包括進行臨牀前研究與臨牀試驗，是一項非常耗時、資金密集且不確定的過程，需要數年才能完成。自成立以來，我們的運作已消耗大量現金，且預期隨著我們識別、繼續研究與開發、啟動與進行臨牀試驗，以及尋求任何產品候選物的監管核准，費用將增加。此外，若我們取得任何產品候選物的監管核准，我們預期將產生與產品銷售、行銷、製造與分銷相關的重大商業化費用，除非這些銷售、行銷、製造與分銷責任由合作夥伴承擔。由於任何臨牀試驗或臨牀前研究的結果極其不確定，我們無法合理預估成功完成產品候選物開發與商業化所需的實際資金數額。其他未預見的費用也可能產生。此外，我們預期將產生與作為上市公司運作相關的額外費用。因此，我們將需要取得大量額外資金以支應持續運作。若我們無法在需要時籌集資金或以可接受的條件籌集資金，我們將被迫延遲、減少或終止研究與產品開發計畫、未來商業化努力或其他運作。
